issue.title: test_global_state_leak_detector nested-pytest nodes hit 60s subprocess timeouts under the loaded full lane
issue.description:
Proposed by phase sase-1vd.4--1 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #2) of epic sase-1vd; filed by the sase-1vd land agent.

The phase's `sase tool run check` full lane failed only on two nodes in `tests/test_global_state_leak_detector.py`, both as 60 s subprocess timeouts under xdist load (worker gw5):

- `tests/test_global_state_leak_detector.py::test_fail_on_poison_mode_fails_pytest_on_poison`
- `tests/test_global_state_leak_detector.py::test_protocol_drain_clears_refresh_thread_restarted_after_fixtures`

Both passed 3/3 in isolation on the phase tree and on the clean base tree. The whole detector file plus the phase's new tests also passed together under `-n 4` (38 passed). The phase diff (question pane cues) touched no leak-detector code.

The phase attributed these to sase-t6. The land agent did not treat them as a duplicate: sase-t6 tracks a different node (`test_snapshot_includes_live_config_token_refresh_threads`) failing on thread-count state, while these are nested-pytest subprocess timeouts. If triage finds a shared root (host load starving the nested pytest subprocess), merge them.

Investigate whether the nested-pytest subprocess these nodes spawn needs a load-aware budget or a semantic wait, rather than only raising the 60 s timeout.

task_type_fields.evidence: 1 full-lane failure of both test_fail_on_poison_mode_fails_pytest_on_poison and test_protocol_drain_clears_refresh_thread_restarted_after_fixtures (60s subprocess timeouts, gw5) during sase-1vd.4--1 on 2026-11-26; 3/3 isolated passes on the phase tree and on the clean base; 38 passed with the file under -n 4. Not reproduced serially.
